title: Global random numbers (Random.h)
recap: A header that defines a generator needs the inline keyword so every file that includes it shares one instance instead of getting its own copy. The same rule that makes shared constants safe makes a shared engine safe.

Wrapping the engine and its distribution in a small namespace gives callers one obvious function: Random::get(min, max). Callers never touch the engine directly, and a fixed seed keeps the whole program reproducible.
objectives: Implement Random::get from its behavioral contract.
Practice the lesson construct by writing the control flow yourself.
Handle multiple inputs and edge cases without hard-coded example answers.
warnings: The examples are not the whole test suite; implement the general behavior.
Do not edit the test drivers. Only the supplied public function signatures are fixed.
Console output and exact source tokens are not graded.
challenge: Implement Random::reset(unsigned int seed) and Random::get(int min, int max) in random.h. reset reseeds one shared inline std::mt19937; get returns the next uniform integer in the INCLUSIVE range, advancing that same engine. Use std::uniform_int_distribution<int>. Calls from different .cpp files must share the sequence, not get separate engines. Inputs always have min <= max and a power-of-two range size (1, 2, 4, or 8); no invalid-range handling is required.
expectedOutput: Resetting to the same seed replays the sequence.
The next call from another .cpp file continues the same sequence.
hints: Define the engine as an inline namespace variable in the header.
reset calls the engine seed member; get must not reseed it.
Construct a distribution for the requested range and invoke it on the shared engine.
